answer: At registration, each agent bonds 40 tokens to a unique hardware root. The operator runs a signature check against that root; on failure, the bond is slashed. When a receipt is submitted, the validator compares the receipt hash to the initial commitment and broadcasts the echo to the network. If a clone appears, it holds only the 3 token reward while the original bond sits at 40, so the forger loses 37 tokens per extra identity. This bridge between hardware and ledger ensures the lantern state remains consistent; the verifier confirms the match at epoch close.
